ŠÀ.GUD: ŠÀ.GUD, a Sumerogram of two signs, ŠÀ + GUD, a worker hired for a yearly wage of grain, whose Akkadian name I cannot read; “ox-driver, ploughman” is only a guess from the signs (ŠÀ “heart, inside” + GUD “ox”) and from the plough that follows in §259, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
epinnum: plough (written with the Sumerogram GIŠ.APIN, the wood-determinative + APIN “plough”; Harper’s List no. 108): epinnam (accusative) “a plough”, epinnim (genitive) “of the plough”: bēl epinnim “the owner of the plough”; the case ending is supplied from the grammar, not written
GIŠ.APIN.TUK.KIN: GIŠ.APIN.TUK.KIN, a Sumerogram of four signs, GIŠ + APIN + TUK + KIN, the name of a farm implement stolen with or beside the plough (§260); a compound of “plough” + TUK + KIN that I cannot read, left unread, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
GIŠ.GAN.UR: GIŠ.GAN.UR, a Sumerogram of three signs, GIŠ + GAN + UR, the name of a second farm implement (§260), left unread, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
nāqidum: herdsman, keeper of flocks (written NA.KAD, the signs NA + KAD, as Harper’s glossary gives it; the identification of the sign group is old and may be superseded): nāqidam (accusative, no ending written) “a herdsman”, hired ana LID.GUD.ZUN u ṣênê rīm “to pasture cattle and sheep”; the case ending is supplied
rêʾûm-pasture: to pasture, graze (a herd): the infinitive in the genitive after ana, ana … rēʾîm “to pasture” (ri-im), said rēʾîm; the spelling ri-im is Harper’s and the reading of the word as the infinitive of rêʾûm (the verb behind rēʾûm “shepherd”) is my own from the grammar, UNCERTAIN
ḫarratum: UNCERTAIN, not read: ḫarratim (ḫar-ra-tim, after a damaged stretch) in the herdsman’s wage clause: idīšu … ḫarratim maḫir “has received his wage … ḫarratim”; Harper marks this word and the mimma before it with his own (?), the stone is damaged here, and I do not know the word, so the unit leaves the damaged phrase untranslated; the lemma is only a placeholder for Harper’s spelling
ṭābum: to be good, pleasing: ṭāb (ṭa-ab, stative, 3rd singular) “is good”: libbašu ṭāb “his heart is good”, i.e. he is satisfied, content
ṣeḫērum-D: D-stem (?) of ṣeḫērum “to be small”: to make small, diminish (the herd): uṣṣaḫḫir (uz-za-aḫ-ḫi-ir, with uz- for uṣ-) “he has diminished”: liātim uṣṣaḫḫir ṣēnī uṣṣaḫḫir “he has made the cattle fewer, he has made the sheep fewer”; the identification is UNCERTAIN, from the grammar and the sense next to maṭûm-D “to reduce”; the form fits a D-stem only loosely, and Harper’s glossary lists it under an intransitive stem, “to be diminished”, which would make the animals the ones that dwindle
talittum: young, offspring (of the herd), from walādum “to bear”: talittam (ta-li-id-tam, accusative) “the young”, the increase of the flock, owed with the biltum “yield”: talittam u biltam inaddin “he shall give the young and the yield”; the stem w of walādum is lost in the noun
ṣarārum-D: UNCERTAIN: uṣarrirma (u-ṣa-ar-ri-ir-ma, D-stem preterite + -ma) “he has been dishonest (?), and”, of the herdsman who cheats; taken as a D-stem of ṣarārum “to be dishonest” (Harper’s glossary: ṣarāru II, “to be dishonest”) from the sense of the law (he changes the mark and sells the animals), not certain
šimtum: mark, brand (?): šimtam (ši-im-tam, accusative) “the mark”, in šimtam uttakkir “he has changed the mark”, a herdsman altering the brand of the animals before selling them; the sense “mark” is UNCERTAIN, taken from the context, and may be the same word as šīmtum “fate, what is fixed”; the spelling does not show the vowel length
nakārum-D: D-stem of nakārum “to be strange, different”: to make different, change: uttakkir (ut-ta-ak-ki-ir, D perfect) “he has changed”: šimtam uttakkir “he has changed the mark (?)” (the object is UNCERTAIN; the verb is plain from the stem)
tarbaṣum: cattle-pen, fold: tarbaṣim (tar-ba-ṣi-im, genitive and after ina) “(in) the pen”: ina tarbaṣim “in the pen”; bēl tarbaṣim “the owner of the pen”; miqitti tarbaṣim “the loss of the pen”; the sign ṣi is the one Harper numbers 72, keyed ZI
liptum: a touch, stroke, blow (from lapātum “to touch”; Harper’s glossary: liptu “stroke, visitation”): lipit (li-bi-it, with BI read as pi, construct) ilim “a stroke of the god”, a plague or sickness sent by the god among the herd, taken here as a sudden affliction (?); the form lipit is a construct before ilim, UNCERTAIN in meaning (“plague”)
ebēbum-D: D-stem of ebēbum “to be clean, pure”: to clear (of blame), declare clean: ubbamma (u-ub-ba-am-ma, D-stem + -ma) “he shall clear himself, and”, before the god; the sense is Harper’s, and the form is UNCERTAIN (I take it for the D-stem with the final b of the stem assimilated to the m of -ma, ubbab-ma > ubbamma; the spelling does not fit fully)
miqittum: loss, fall, what has fallen: miqitti (mi-qi₂-it-ti, construct) “the loss of” (the KI of the spelling is read qi), from maqātum “to fall”: miqitti tarbaṣim “the loss of the pen”, the animals lost to the plague or the lion; the sign values are mi-qi₂-it-ti
kazzatum: UNCERTAIN: kazzatam (ka-az-za-tam, accusative), kazzatim (genitive), a word for some harm or mishap in the pen brought about by a careless herdsman (Harper’s glossary: kazzatu “injury”); the spelling is ka + az + za + tam; “a harm (?)” is a guess from the sense of the clause, and the word is left as kazzatum
ḫiditum: UNCERTAIN: ḫidit (ḫi-di-it, construct) “the … of”, followed by kazzatim: the “loss (?)” the herdsman must make good; Harper’s glossary has a word “blame, reproach, disaster, loss” for it; the meaning is guessed from the parallel with miqitti in §266, and the word is left as ḫiditum
dīāšum: threshing: dīāšim (di-a-ši-im, genitive after ana) “for threshing”, said of hired animals (ox, donkey, a small animal) used to tread out the grain: ana dīāšim īgur “he has hired for threshing”; the infinitive of dâšum “to thresh”, used as a noun
lalûm: UNCERTAIN: LÁ-am, lalâm (accusative), a hired animal in the threshing rates beside the ox and the donkey, hired for 1 qa of grain; written LÁ (the sign “to hang, to weigh”) + AM, read lalâm; Harper’s glossary has “small animal, goat (?)”, which fits the very low price, but the word is not certain
ṣumbum: wagon, cart: ṣumbam (GIŠ.MAR.GÍD.DA, accusative), ṣumbamma (GIŠ.MAR.GÍD.DA-ma, accusative + -ma) “the wagon only”, a Sumerogram of four signs (GIŠ + MAR + GÍD + DA, “long wagon”) read in Akkadian; the sign GÍD is keyed LAL, tentative; ṣumbum is my reading of the Sumerogram from its sense (a hired wagon with its driver), UNCERTAIN
murteddûm: driver, one who drives (the cattle and the wagon): murteddīša (mu-ur-te-di-ša, with the suffix -ša “its”) “its driver”, taken as a participle of redûm “to lead, drive” in the Gt-stem (the infix -t- after the first radical), UNCERTAIN in the stem; the cattle, the wagon and its driver are hired together at the higher day-rate
180: one hundred and eighty — the sexagesimal numeral 3 × 60 (three 60-wedges): said šalāš šūšī (?) “three sixties”, with qa “180 qa of grain” per day; the spoken form is reconstructed
40: forty — four corner-wedges (4 × 10): said erbâ (?) “forty”, with qa “40 qa of grain” per day; the spoken form is reconstructed
ḫamšum: fifth: ḫamšim (ḫa-am-ši-im, genitive, before ITI “month”), ḫamšim warḫim “the fifth month”, the end of the first period of the year in the hired man’s rates
šeššum: sixth: šeššim (ši-ši-im, genitive, before ITI “month”), šeššim warḫim “the sixth month”, the start of the second period of the year; from the numeral šeššet “six”
taktida: UNCERTAIN: ta-ak-ti-da, a word after adi “until” in the rate of the hired man, ištu rēš šattim adi ḫamšim warḫim … ištu šeššim warḫim adi taktida šattim “from the start of the year until the fifth month … from the sixth month until the taktida of the year”; I take it as a word for the end of the year (“the close, the end (?)”) from the context and do not know the form; left unread
GAB.A: GAB.A, a Sumerogram of two signs, GAB + A, with the person-determinative {lu₂} before it: the name of a craftsman or trade in the hire-list of §274, paid 5 še of silver a day; I cannot read it in Akkadian and leave it unread, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
KAD: KAD, a Sumerogram, a single sign with the person-determinative {lu₂}: a craftsman’s trade in the hire-list of §274, paid 5 še a day (the numeral is restored by Harper, in brackets); the same sign is the second of NA.KAD “herdsman” (see nāqidum); I cannot read the word and leave it unread, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
GUL: GUL, a Sumerogram, a single sign with the person-determinative {lu₂}: a craftsman’s trade in the hire-list of §274, the amount lost; the sign means “to destroy, to hew”, and I do not read the word, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
GA: GA(?), a single sign (GA) with the person-determinative {lu₂} and Harper’s own question mark, a trade in the hire-list of §274, the amount lost; the identification of the sign is Harper’s and doubtful, and the word is left unread, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
nangarum: carpenter, joiner (written with the single sign NAGAR; Harper’s glossary gives the sign two words, nangaru “carpenter” and agru “hired man”): nangarim (nan-garim, genitive, as Harper prints it; the plate has NAGAR alone) “of a carpenter”, in the hire-list of §274: idi … nangarim 4 še kaspim “the hire of a … carpenter, 4 grains of silver”; the same sign with the person-determinative is Harper’s agrum “hireling” in §273 (see agrum), and the two readings are told apart by the context only; Harper’s form is kept (a later normalization of the carpenter is naggārum)
SA: SA, a Sumerogram, a single sign, a trade in the hire-list of §274, paid 4 še of silver a day (the numeral is restored in brackets, UNCERTAIN); the sign means “net, sinew, cord”, and the word is not read, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
AT.KIT: AT.KIT, a Sumerogram of two signs, AT + KIT, a trade in the hire-list of §274, the amount lost; I cannot read it in Akkadian and leave it unread, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given

__broaden__.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading) · bēlišu (be-li-šu) “its owner” (of an animal), bēlišuma “to its owner only” (with the emphatic -ma); bēl alpim “the owner of the ox” · bēl epinnim “the owner of the plough”, bēl tarbaṣim “the owner of the pen”; bēlīšunu (be-li-šu-nu) “their owners”, the owners of the cattle and sheep a herdsman has lost
__broaden__.rēʾûm: shepherd — here written with the Sumerogram SIPA · herdsman of cattle and sheep, the hired man of §264–267, written SIPA: rēʾûm “the herdsman” (rēʾûm, in the lost-herd laws); the signs are the same as for “shepherd”, and the Akkadian says herdsman as well
__broaden__.bašûm: to exist, arise: ibbaššû “which arose” · lā ibaššišum “there is not to him” (= he has none), with dative -šum · in broken forms …ši (ul ibašši, “there is not”, the verb itself restored); ibaššû “which are (there)”, in mimma ina qātīšu ibaššû · ibašši (i-ba-aš-ši, present) “there is, is upon”: ḫubullum elišu ibašši “a debt is upon him” · ittabši (it-tab-ši, perfect) “has happened, has broken out”, of the plague in the pen: lipit ilim ittabši “a stroke of the god has happened”
__broaden__.dâkum: to kill; N-stem iddâk “he shall be killed” — the code’s death sentence · idukkū (i-du-uk-ku) “they shall kill” (active plural, unlike the N-stem iddâk) · iddūkšu (id-du-uk-šu) “has killed him/it”, taken as the perfect + -šu, the doubled d being the perfect’s infix -ta- assimilated to the root’s d (so read; UNCERTAIN in form) · iddūk (id-du-uk) “has killed”, of the lion in the pen, nēšum iddūk “a lion has killed”; the form is read as the perfect (iddūk with the infix -ta- assimilated, as in iddūkšu), not as the N-stem iddâk “he shall be killed”, UNCERTAIN in form
__broaden__.maḫārum: to receive: imḫur(u) · imḫur, imḫuru “he received” (preterite; subjunctive in a clause), imaḫḫar “he shall receive” (present); …ḫari… in a broken form · to face, withstand (litany): qabal lā maḫārim “combat none can face” · imtaḫar (im-ta-ḫar) “she received” (perfect; Harper’s maḫāru I,2, “to receive”): grain and silver for beer · maḫir (ma-ḫi-ir, stative, 3rd singular) “has received”: idīšu … maḫir “he has received his wage” · imaḫḫaršu (i-maḫ-ḫar-šu, present + -šu) “he shall accept from him”: the owner of the pen imaḫḫaršu the loss, “shall accept it from him”
__broaden__.pûm: mouth (the KA sign); ina pī mātim “in the mouth of the land” · ana pî ṣimdat šarrim “according to the mouth of the king’s ordinance” · ana pî riksātīšu “according to his contract”, literally “to the mouth of his binding terms” (KA read pî)
__broaden__.rēšum: head, top · rēš šattim (ri-eš ša-at-tim) “the start of the year”, literally “the head of the year”: ištu rēš šattim “from the start of the year”
__broaden__.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …” · ūmīšu (UD-mi-šu) “his days”: ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days” · ina ūmim (i-na UD) “per day, by the day”, with the numeral 1{kam}: ina ūmim 1{kam} 180 qa “for each day 180 qa”; the day-rate formula of §271–277
__broaden__.ramānum: self: ramānšu ipaddar “he shall redeem himself” · ana ramānīša (ra-ma-ni-ša) “by itself, for itself”, of the wagon hired alone: ṣumbamma ana ramānīša “the wagon only, by itself”
__broaden__.6: six — six vertical wedges (6): šeššet “six” before šeʾum, where the 6 counts the barleycorns (še) that make up the fraction of a shekel · šeššet “six” before kur: 6 ŠE.GUR “six kor of grain”, the herdsman’s wage; and before ŠE: 6 ŠE “six še (grains)” of silver, the day-rate of §273
__broaden__.1: one — a single vertical wedge (DIŠ): 1 mana “one mina” · ištēt (?) “one” with the feminine šattum, a reconstructed spoken form: ana šattim ištēt “for one year”; also written 1{kam} · ištēn (?) “one” with a masculine noun, a reconstructed spoken form: 1 qa šeʾim “one qa of grain”
__broaden__.šeʾum: barley, grain (the ŠE sign) · ŠE-am, ŠE-im, ŠE-um, written with the logogram and a spelled vowel; šeʾum as the subject; ŠE-am-ma “grain only” (with the restricting -ma); in broken forms še… · ŠE alone, as a small silver weight, the še “grain”, one hundred and eightieth of a shekel: 5 ŠE kaspim “five še of silver”, the day-rates of §273–277
__broaden__.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost” · “in proportion to”: kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share”, kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house” · in place of, for (of animal for animal): alpam kīma alpim “an ox for an ox” (the §263 restitution)
__broaden__.1-kam: one, written 1{kam}: the numeral 1 followed by the sign KAM, written raised ({kam}), as in the earlier counts of years; said ištēt (?) with the feminine šattum: MU 1{kam} “one year”, ištēt reconstructed · ištēn (?) with the masculine ūmum, a reconstructed spoken form: ina ūmim 1{kam} “per day” (UD 1{kam}), the day-rate formula of §271–277 (ūmum is masculine, so the masculine form; šattum, feminine, takes ištēt)
__broaden__.agrum: hired man, hireling: {amēlu}agram “a hireling” (the person-determinative + the sign Harper’s list reads agru) · {lu₂}NAGAR (§273): the sign NAGAR with the person-determinative, agram “a hireling” (accusative); Harper’s glossary gives the sign NAGAR two words, agru “hired man” (here) and nangaru “carpenter” (§274, see nangarum); a modern edition reads the hireling as ḪUN.GÁ
__broaden__.agārum: to hire: īgurma “he hired, and” · īgur (i-gur) “he hired”, without -ma, and īguru (i-gu-ru) “(who) hired”, with the relative -u: awīlum ša alpam īguru “the man who hired the ox” · īgur (i-gur) “he has hired”, the plain preterite of the hire-laws of §258–277 · iggar (i-ig-ga-ar) “he hires”, a present, Harper’s reading in §274 (the spelling with the extra i is not explained, UNCERTAIN)
__broaden__.bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect) · uštabši (uš-tab-ši) “he has brought about” (perfect): kazzatam uštabši “he has brought about a harm (?)” · ušabšû (u-ša-ab-šu-u) “which he brought about” (preterite + relative -u)
__broaden__.maḫirtum: UNCERTAIN: a kind of boat, sense unknown: maḫirtim (ma-ḫi-ir-tim, genitive; Harper restores part of the word in §240): ša maḫirtim “the one of the maḫirtu”, elippum ša maḫirtim “a boat of the maḫirtu” · noun, sense uncertain · maḫirtam (ma-ḫi-ir-tam, accusative), the object of īgur in §276: šumma maḫirtam īgur “if he has hired a maḫirtu”
__broaden__.idum: hire, wages (Harper: ID, the ideogram for hire): idi našpakim “the hire of the bin”, written with the single sign Á (A₂, “arm; hire”); the case ending is not written, so idi (construct, before a genitive) is an assumed reading, UNCERTAIN · idīšu (Á-šu, with -šu “his”) “his fee”, the physician’s pay: ana asîm idīšu “to the physician as his fee”; the case vowel is UNCERTAIN · Á alone, no ending and no suffix written, before a named kind of ox: idi GU₄.DA.UR.RA “the hire of a GU₄.DA.UR.RA”; the plate sign is Á (A₂), where Harper prints ID · idīša (Á-ša) “her hire”, idīšu (Á-šu) “its hire”, of a thing hired (a boat, an ox, a donkey), -ša / -šu agreeing with the thing; the case vowel is UNCERTAIN · idi (Á, construct) before a trade name: idi GAB.A “the hire of a GAB.A”, the hire-list of §274
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him” · nadānam (na-da-nam, infinitive accusative) “to give”: warkassa … nadānam “(that she may) give her estate” · iddišši (id-di-iš-ši) “he gave her”, preterite + -ši, the n written š: ana mutim iddišši “he gave her to a husband” · inaddinūši (i-na-ad-di-nu-ši) “they shall give her”, inaddinūšimma (i-na-ad-di-nu-šim-ma) “they shall give her, and”, ittadnūšimma (it-ta-ad-nu-ši-im-ma) “they have given her, and” (perfect plural + -šim + -ma) · iddinušim (id-di-nu-ši-im) “he gave her”, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause · inaddiššum (i-na-ad-di-iš-šum) “he shall give him” (inaddin + -šum, the n assimilated to š) · innadnušum (in-na-ad-nu-šum) “were given to him” (N-stem preterite + relative -u + -šum): ša innadnušum “that was given to him” · ittadin (it-ta-di-in) “he has given” (perfect): ana kaspim ittadin “he has sold for silver”
